question: Which initial safety ceilings bound each first-vertical WebAssembly invocation?
selected_option: Balanced first-vertical ceilings: 64 MiB linear memory, 8,192 table elements, one instance, 4 MiB input, 4 MiB output, 256 KiB structured logs, 50 million deterministic fuel units, a 5-second wall watchdog, and two concurrent component invocations per daemon.
rationale: The user explicitly selected OPT-WASM-BUDGET-BALANCED. It supplies bounded room for non-trivial pure-proposal analysis without adopting the substantially larger resource and responsiveness exposure of the throughput profile.

required_semantics: all ceilings apply before or during allocation and execution; exceeding any ceiling fails the invocation closed
input, output, and log limits apply to decoded canonical payload bytes so compression or framing cannot bypass them
fuel exhaustion deterministically traps the invocation under the exact pinned Wasmtime configuration
the wall watchdog cancels or traps overlong execution as defense in depth and does not define a deterministic instruction point
cancellation, traps, deadline expiry, excess output, or resource refusal produce no partial proposal and no accepted-state mutation
the daemon applies bounded queueing and rejects excess work rather than exceeding the two-invocation concurrency ceiling
benchmark and conformance evidence may lower any ceiling; increasing a ceiling requires a new reviewed decision
a Wasmtime or compilation-configuration change invalidates fuel calibration and requires renewed budget evidence
non_implications: the selected ceilings are not latency, throughput, capacity, compatibility, or user-experience guarantees
the selected ceilings do not prove representative components complete within them
the selected ceilings do not satisfy the pending WebAssembly security-owner gate
this decision does not authorize implementation, component execution, resource reservation, release, or deployment
